subject: coyote
title: A Coyote and a Badger Hunt Together, and the Squirrels Lose

scenes.text: A coyote and a badger hunt side by side. Neither one is the prey.
They both eat ground squirrels, and a squirrel has two escapes: run, or dive underground.
The badger digs straight down after it, so the squirrel bolts out another exit.
In Wyoming, coyotes hunting with a badger caught about a third more squirrels than coyotes alone.
Stay below, meet the badger. Run, meet the coyote. That's why they hunt together.

description:
Coyotes and American badgers sometimes hunt ground squirrels and prairie dogs together: the badger digs into the burrows while the coyote waits for anything that runs out.
A study on Wyoming's National Elk Refuge found coyotes hunting with a badger caught about 34 percent more ground squirrels per hour than solitary coyotes, and the badgers likely gain too.
Which animal partnership surprised you most?
first_comment: Both species have also been seen killing each other's young. Partners or rivals?
